## VO Capture & Control — all-in-one workflow

**Client:** `MASTER` (template — this copy runs nothing)
**App:** `https://vo.osmanflow.com`

One file, one import, every lane. Node names carry their lane letter so a
failed execution names the lane before anything has to be opened.

### Before this file is a client's workflow — the duplication checklist

1. **Rebind every credential.** Gmail, Google Drive. Credentials do NOT travel
   with an export; the fields look filled and are not.
2. **Regenerate every webhook path.** Two clients sharing `vo/whatsapp` means
   one contractor's site photos land in another contractor's register.
3. **Rebind the three secret-bearing credentials** — `VO · sign requests to the
   app`, `VO · verify requests from the app`, `VO · Evolution API`. The two
   crypto ones must hold EXACTLY the app's `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and
   `N8N_OUTBOUND_SECRET`. ⚠️ `.env.production` quotes its values; strip the
   quotes. A secret with quotes around it is a different secret, and the only
   symptom is a 401 saying "Invalid request signature".
4. **Change the four plain values** at the top of the generator: the app URL,
   the Evolution URL and instance, and the Drive folder id. They are not
   secrets, and `$env` is NOT available — this instance blocks env access in
   nodes, which is n8n's default.
5. **Point Evolution's webhook** at lane A's production URL, event
   `MESSAGES_UPSERT` only.
6. **Set this workflow as its own Error Workflow** in Settings, or lane H never
   fires.
7. **Import deactivated. Test each lane. Then activate.**

⚠️ Activation is all-or-nothing — that is the cost of one file per client.
Lane H routes failures by letter so the cost is bearable.

## How a request is signed, and why it is fussy

Every call to the app carries `x-vo-timestamp` and `x-vo-signature`, an
HMAC-SHA256 over the string `timestamp.rawBody` — the exact bytes, not the
object.

**So the body is sent as `raw`, never as `json`.** If the HTTP node were left
on JSON body it would re-serialise the object, key order and spacing could
differ by one byte from what was hashed, and every request would fail
verification with a message about the signature that says nothing about the
cause. The Code node builds the string; the Crypto node signs that string; the
HTTP node sends that same string.

**The key lives in a Crypto credential, never in a node parameter.** Crypto v2
has no `secret` field at all — an earlier draft set one and n8n silently ignored
it, so every Sign node rendered with an empty box and would have signed with
nothing. Two credentials, because the two directions use different keys:
`VO · sign requests to the app` for outbound, `VO · verify requests from the
app` for what the app sends here.

**The Code nodes run once for ALL items, so `$json` is undefined in them.** They
read `$input.first().json`. `$json` there is not a style preference — it is a
node that throws the moment a real message arrives.

### Lane A · WhatsApp in (Evolution)
**Trigger:** Evolution posts `MESSAGES_UPSERT` here.
**Calls:** `POST /api/integrations/whatsapp/incoming-message`
**Idempotency:** `evolution:<message id>` — Evolution retries, and a retry must
not create a second Potential Change.

**This lane must never:** decide which project a message belongs to. It carries
the sender's phone; the app resolves identity and memberships. A courier that
guesses at a project is how a claim ends up on the wrong job.

crypto.name: VO · sign requests to the app

parameters.content:
### Lane B · Email in
**Trigger:** Gmail, unread in the VO mailbox.
**Calls:** `POST /api/integrations/email/incoming-email`
**Idempotency:** the Gmail message id.

**Bound to the `Gmail account` credential.** The mailbox has not been chosen yet.
Swap this node for IMAP if the client is not on Google.

**This lane must never:** mark a mail read before the app has accepted it. A
mail marked read on a failed POST is a change nobody ever sees again.

crypto.name: VO · sign requests to the app

parameters.content:
### Lane C · Document watch
**Trigger:** a file appears in the project's Drive folder.
**Calls:** `POST /api/integrations/documents/uploaded`
**Idempotency:** the Drive file id.

`project_code` is read from the folder path. A file the app cannot place is
rejected with a 4xx — it does not become a document on a guessed project.

crypto.name: VO · sign requests to the app

parameters.content:
### Lane D · Email out
**Trigger:** the app posts a queued notification here.
**Sends:** Gmail.
**Then:** reports back to `/api/integrations/notifications/delivery-status`.

**The callback is the point.** The app marks a row `queued` when it hands the
message over, never `sent`. Only D9 can move it to delivered. Without that,
the app would claim a notice was delivered on the strength of its own outbound
request — which is exactly the claim that loses an argument later.

**Bound to the `Gmail account` credential.**

crypto.name: VO · verify requests from the app

parameters.errorMessage: Lane D: request signature did not verify

crypto.name: VO · sign requests to the app

parameters.content:
### Lane E · WhatsApp out (Evolution)
**Trigger:** the app posts a queued WhatsApp notification here.
**Sends:** `POST {VO_EVOLUTION_URL}/message/sendText/{VO_EVOLUTION_INSTANCE}`
**Then:** reports delivery back, same as lane D.

⚠️ **Use a SEPARATE Evolution instance from the outreach number.** Cold
outreach on Baileys carries a real ban risk, and a ban is permanent. Sharing
one number means the day outreach gets the number banned is the day the
product stops telling anyone about their notice deadlines.

crypto.name: VO · verify requests from the app

### Lane S · The schedules
Everything this system does on a clock lives here, so it can be seen, paused
and proved from one screen.

| When | Job |
|---|---|
| 07:00 daily | `reminder_sweep` — who is late, who gets chased, who gets escalated |
| Every 30 min, 07–19 | `notification_dispatch` — messages a lane could not take earlier |
| 06:00 daily | `bottleneck_sweep` — what is blocked and how much is waiting on it |

**What did NOT move here: deciding who is owed what.** That stays in the app,
where the escalation ladder and the dedupe key are tested. As n8n nodes it
would be a diagram nobody can run twice safely, and a retried execution would
chase the same project manager twice. A system that double-chases gets muted.

**`If Execution Is Missed` is set to run the most recent missed execution.**
A deploy at 07:00 must not cost a day of chasing.

**Safe to fire twice.** Each job reads current state and works out what is owed
now; the dedupe key covers task, kind, day, channel and recipient.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ts: String(Date.now()), payload: JSON.stringify({ job: 'reminder_sweep' }) } }];

### Lane H · Errors
Catches a failure in any lane above and names the lane before anything else has
to be opened — the whole reason node names carry a letter.

Routing by lane letter is what makes one file per client bearable: the
execution list mixes eight lanes together, and without this you would be
reading a stack trace to find out which one broke.

⚠️ Set this workflow as its own **Error Workflow** in Settings, or nothing
reaches here.

### Lanes F and G · not built yet, on purpose

**F · Client follow-up** and **G · Weekly report** are in the lane map and are
deliberately absent from this file.

Both need an app endpoint that does not exist yet. F chases a client for a
response to a notice — and the app cannot yet issue a notice, so there is
nothing to chase. G delivers a weekly commercial report the app cannot yet
produce.

Building the couriers now would mean nodes wired to URLs that 404, which pass
validation, sit in the workflow looking finished, and fail on the first day
anyone relies on them. They arrive with the stage that gives them something to
carry.
